scope_note: Full public-evidence account for the Google Bridgeport/Jackson County campus, keyed to one selected inventory building but preserving every source at campus, named taxpayer-account, company-county, recipient, utility-region or state scope. The account separates nine projections from reported actuals; preserves three non-additive cumulative investment snapshots; retains the full 2020-2025 appraised, assessed and paid-tax histories for three exact-address accounts; marks grant and workforce overlap; and rejects unsupported building allocation, vendor spending, realized payroll, permit valuation, tax-abatement amounts, public costs and net fiscal claims. Source-reported environmental values, project boundaries and the direct-payroll forecast are governed direct records; only residual calculations and source-modeled economic outputs remain modeled.

sources.title: Coming home to Alabama
sources.notes: Contemporaneous construction announcement: $600 million planned investment, as many as 100 high-skilled jobs, a planned $100,000 school-district donation, reuse of Widows Creek transmission infrastructure, and a renewable-energy commitment. sources.title: How Google’s Search Ended in Alabama

sources.title: Google Strengthens Alabama Presence With New Data Center Investment, Community Initiatives

project_updates.title: Operator chronology, investment and boundary audit
project_updates.notes: Reviewed the 2018 groundbreaking, current location page, 2024 impact study and June 2026 expansion release. Retained separately the $600 million original plan, TVA's approximately $600 million FY2020 capital-program result, the greater-than-$980 million 2024 historical snapshot, current greater-than-$2 billion Alabama snapshot, and $1.5 billion 2026-2027 expansion plan; none is summed or allocated to the selected building. The 2018 location-page opening milestone conflicts with the 2026 release's 2019 operations start, so both are preserved as a chronology conflict.
project_updates.project_description: Google operates a data-center campus at the retired Widows Creek coal-plant site in Bridgeport, Jackson County, Alabama; the selected inventory building is only one unallocated part of that campus. Google broke ground in 2018, while its current location page says the first center opened in 2018 and its June 2026 release says campus operations began in 2019. OSHA's 2018 construction partnership describes a 465 +/- acre project planned for multiple two-story 60 MW facilities with exterior electrical and mechanical cooling plants, and names Holder Construction Group as construction manager.

project_updates.title: Assessor and tax-payment evidence matrix
project_updates.notes: Queried owner Google and exact address 48809 AL Hwy 277 in the Jackson County Revenue Commissioner portal. Retained every 2020-2025 appraised value, assessed value and paid tax for accounts 151335/PPIN 50326 (Google), 151342/PPIN 50327 (Design), and 151344/PPIN 50328 (Wiessner); Google is named in payment memos on the two non-Google accounts in 2021-2024, and Design's Google subsidiary status is independently documented. Excluded the three accounts' unpaid 2026 estimates and exact-address ADP and Schenker results because no project relationship was established. The corrective pass reproduced the actual company-search POST, enumerated all eight Wiessner real parcels under account 98353, and preserved separate 2020-2025 appraisal, assessment, billed-tax and paid-tax histories; recipient distribution, an abated-tax counterfactual, complete affiliate roster and audit of entities not discoverable through the portal remain unresolved.

project_updates.title: Incentive, public-cost and debt gap closure
project_updates.notes: Searched Alabama Revenue Chapter 9B guidance, Alabama Commerce/ADECA records, Alabama Examiners audit search and Jackson County Commission agendas/minutes for 2018-2026. Program rules confirm possible 10-, 20- or 30-year data-center abatements and require an executed agreement. The corrective pass later found 2015 county resolutions approving and amending a Wiessner Master Project Agreement, but still no agreement text, schedules, compliance report, certified $50 million investment-credit value, $20 million sales-tax abatement, $11.8 million property-tax abatement, or $109 million ten-year state impact figure in a primary project record; those secondary-source figures remain rejected. No allocated project infrastructure cost, operating subsidy, debt, bond, reimbursement, clawback, tax-recipient allocation or same-scope marginal service cost was located; net fiscal modeling is ineligible, while exact annual tax aggregation and an equal-cost threshold are eligible.

project_updates.title: Planning, permit, contractor and supplier search
project_updates.notes: Reviewed OSHA Partnership 907, TVA Widows Creek disposition records, Jackson County indexed agendas/minutes, operator releases and local planning/permit search results. OSHA supplies 465 +/- acres, multiple two-story facilities, 60 MW per facility, Holder construction management and major MEP/steel/precast/site-work categories; TVA separately reports 566 acres sold. The corrective assessor pass later supplied three campus improvement areas and building counts, but no certificate of occupancy, selected-building crosswalk, construction contract payment, supplier invoice, local vendor payment, residence share, wage ledger or procurement spend. The 60 MW per-facility projection and distinct site boundaries are cataloged without summing or allocating them.

project_updates.title: Utility, load, generation and resource search
project_updates.notes: Reviewed Google releases/location materials, TVA annual and Widows Creek records, ADEM eFile/EPA facility search, and available Bridgeport/Jackson County water records. Retained 2024 withdrawal of approximately 201.6 million gallons and direct 2022-2024 consumption/discharge/PUE/CFE values without allocating a building. More than 300 MW contracted regional generation and up to 50 MW shared Tennessee/Alabama advanced nuclear supply are not campus load or facility capacity. The corrective pass later found ECHO identifiers, ADEM facility 705-0057, Title V runtime ceilings and an assessor generator feature count, but still no facility electricity meter/load, tariff payment, interconnection cost, water rate/payment, pollutant quantities, renewable-energy payment or selected-building resource allocation.

project_updates.title: Workforce, operations and compensation evidence matrix
project_updates.notes: Retained separately the up-to-100-job 2018 plan, TVA's nearly-70-job FY2020 result, the 2023 approximately 230 direct-and-indirect job snapshot with an approximately 100-Google-employee component, the greater-than-1,800 historical construction workforce, and the greater-than-1,000-worker 2026 expansion statement. None is converted to FTE, job-years, payroll, wages, benefits, residence or current headcount. Google careers, OSHA, operator releases, state workforce materials and county sources supplied no roster, occupation mix, facility payroll, contractor payroll, hours, union status, turnover or vendor employment ledger, so compensation and further workforce modeling are rejected.

project_updates.title: Source-modeled economic contribution disposition
project_updates.notes: The Deloitte/Google study's annual-average 2021-2023 Alabama outputs are retained only as visibly source-modeled estimates: about $77 million GDP ($42 million direct, $19 million indirect, $16 million induced), about 690 jobs (255/270/165), and about $47 million labor income ($19 million/$20 million/$8 million). Its approximately $520,000 carbon-free-energy GDP and $230,000 labor-income outputs, 42% professional/technical GDP share, 58% other-sector share, 21% modeled GDP growth versus 8% Alabama GDP growth, $2.40 social benefit per dollar, and 2022-2023 environmental percentages receive explicit model disposition rather than direct-actual treatment. The approximately 790 household equivalents are not retained with a jobs surrogate: catalog proposal study.household_income_equivalents needs a households unit and a source-modeled record. The reported 83% PUE-overhead reduction versus 1.58 industry PUE is not a facility contribution or electricity saving; catalog proposal study.pue_overhead_reduction_vs_industry needs percent, benchmark vintage and formula fields before direct/context publication. No building-level allocation, observed payroll, observed supplier spending or causal effect is inferred.

project_updates.title: Community recipient and beneficiary reconciliation
project_updates.notes: Cross-checked operator totals against Mountain Lakes Chamber and NACC recipient records. Retained monetary contributions at their native recipient/period scopes and marked overlap: $50,000 school grant, $100,000 library aggregate, greater than $750,000 local grants, approximately $1.1 million to 22 organizations, greater than $100,000 for NACC, $57,000 for YouScience, and the $2 million/$550,000 2026 announcements. Catalog-and-record proposals are required for nonmonetary outputs: study.community_organizations_supported (organizations: 22), study.community_program_participants (participants/students: about 100 NACC, over 7,500 YouScience in the Google study, 2,221 participation and 1,327 completions in the recipient report, over 60 NACC campers, over 1,500 robotics participants), study.volunteer_hours (hours: over 6,000 statewide), and study.recipient_program_expenditure (USD: $359.24 NACC Google STEM Camp fund expense). No transaction-complete disbursement or overlap ledger was found.

project_updates.title: County GDP, employment and wage design disposition
project_updates.notes: The official-source repository panel has complete positive Jackson County GDP, covered-employment and nominal weekly-wage observations through 2024. The corrective audit reran 2018 and 2019 anchors, national and Southeast donor universes, 3/5/10/20-donor specifications and every leave-one-out case. The declared descriptive gate requires sign stability across all cases and maximum pre-period RMSE below 5 percent. Only nominal weekly wage passes (gap range 0.95 to 6.36 percent; maximum RMSE 1.55 percent) and is retained as descriptive context. Employment changes sign (-6.26 to 4.63 percent; maximum RMSE 8.60) and GDP changes sign (-6.06 to 3.84 percent; maximum RMSE 6.83), so both are retired. No facility wage series, isolated treatment timing, verified uncontaminated donor pool, placebos, spillover rule or causal robustness package was found.

project_updates.title: Adversarial state-project and compensation follow-up

Only the payroll floor is eligible for a deterministic annualized model; the undefined economic-impact aggregate is rejected from synthesis.

Open routes are recipient ledgers, school-board records, fund awards/disbursements, updated county vintages and a defensible identification design.
